questions.question: A developer asks GitHub Copilot Chat to write a log statement for a failed payment. The prompt contains only the instruction. The response uses a generic console.error call instead of the team's custom log format. Which change to the prompt is most likely to produce output in the team's format?

options.text: Include two or three example log lines in the team's format before the request
options.why: Correct. A few-shot prompt shows the model the exact pattern to follow.

options.text: Repeat the same instruction in capital letters
options.why: Emphasis does not tell Copilot what the custom format looks like.

options.text: Switch the chat to Agent mode
options.why: Agent mode changes how Copilot acts on files, not whether it knows the team's format.

options.text: Close all other editor tabs
options.why: Closing unrelated tabs can reduce noise for inline suggestions, but it does not supply the format.

questions.explanation: Adding examples turns a zero-shot prompt into a few-shot prompt, which guides Copilot to the required format.

questions.question: Which statement describes a zero-shot prompt?

options.text: A prompt that contains the instruction without any examples of the expected output
options.why: Correct. Zero-shot prompts rely on the instruction and the available context only.

options.text: A prompt that contains one example of the expected output
options.why: A prompt with exactly one example is a one-shot prompt, a form of few-shot prompting.

options.text: A prompt that is sent with no code context from the editor
options.why: Zero-shot refers to the absence of examples, not the absence of editor context.

options.text: A prompt that Copilot answers without calling the language model
options.why: Every Copilot response is generated by a language model.

questions.explanation: Zero-shot prompting provides the task alone. Few-shot prompting adds examples.

questions.question: A developer is filling a JavaScript file with many similar test cases and wants GitHub Copilot inline suggestions to follow the same structure. The developer does not want to use Copilot Chat. What should the developer do?

options.text: Write the first two test cases manually and place the cursor on the next line
options.why: Correct. Code above the cursor is context for inline suggestions, so the examples act as a few-shot prompt.

options.text: Add the setting github.copilot.enable for JavaScript
options.why: This setting turns completions on or off for a language. It does not teach Copilot a structure.

options.text: Press Ctrl+Enter before writing any code
options.why: The completions panel shows alternatives but does not supply examples of the desired structure.

options.text: Create a content exclusion for the tests folder
options.why: Excluded files do not receive inline suggestions at all.

questions.explanation: Examples written in the file give inline suggestions a pattern to continue.

questions.question: A team wants to improve the quality of GitHub Copilot Chat responses. Which TWO practices follow prompt crafting best practices?

options.text: Limit each prompt to a single, well-defined task
options.why: Correct. Focused prompts produce more accurate answers than combined requests.

options.text: Specify inputs, outputs and rules, such as returning the total unchanged for unknown codes
options.why: Correct. Specific requirements reduce guessing.

options.text: Combine the feature, its tests, documentation and a migration in one prompt
options.why: Combining unrelated tasks usually produces shallow results for each.

options.text: Paste production customer records so that Copilot sees realistic data
options.why: Real personal data must not be included in prompts. Use fake examples instead.

questions.explanation: Effective prompts are focused and specific. Sensitive data should never be pasted into a prompt.

questions.question: A development team found that few-shot prompts produce code in its standard error format. Developers often forget to paste the examples. The format must apply to every Copilot Chat request in the repository. What should the team do?

options.text: Add the format and an example to .github/copilot-instructions.md
options.why: Correct. Repository custom instructions are added to chat requests in the repository automatically.

options.text: Keep one long chat open that contains the examples
options.why: Chat history applies only to that conversation and does not reach other developers or new chats.

options.text: Ask each developer to type the examples at the start of every day
options.why: This depends on people remembering and does not apply automatically.

options.text: Enable the suggestions matching public code policy
options.why: This policy controls suggestions that match public code. It does not apply a team format.

questions.explanation: Custom instructions apply standing rules to every request. Prompt files can store reusable few-shot prompts.
